title: The night that never cools
text: It is two in the morning and her tin-roofed room is still holding the day’s heat. She has barely slept, her body hasn’t recovered from yesterday, and the shift starts at seven.
fact: Hot nights are dangerous because the body gets less chance to recover from the day. Sleep-tracker data from 68 countries shows people sleep about 14 minutes less on nights above 30 °C, with bigger losses for older people and in lower-income countries.

title: Salt in the canal
who: A rice farmer in Viet Nam’s Mekong Delta
text: Before dawn he checks the canal beside his rice. The heat has drawn it low, and the water tastes of salt. Pump it onto the field and he could lose half the crop; wait, and the field dries out. Either way, this season’s loan falls due.
fact: In February 2024 a long heatwave in the Mekong Delta lowered the canals and let sea water push inland. Farmers who pumped the salty water onto their rice lost up to half their crop.

title: The field can’t wait
who: A woman farming rainfed land in Nepal’s Madhesh plains
text: The monsoon is late, and by mid-morning her seedlings are wilting. The seed was bought on credit, so if this crop fails the debt grows. She keeps working the field through the heat.
fact: Heat does not land equally even within farming villages. Rural households headed by women lose about 8% more of their income to heat stress than households headed by men.

title: School closes
text: Her school shuts for the heat again. At home she fetches water and looks after her younger brothers, and after weeks like this her family starts to wonder whether she should go back at all.

title: No shade between orders
text: At midday the road shimmers and the delivery app keeps sending orders. He is paid by the delivery, so every rest in the shade costs him money. Tonight, his rented room has no fan.
fact: In Jakarta, dense low-income neighbourhoods act as heat islands. Informal workers rarely have fans or air conditioning and cool off on terraces or in parks, while green space is concentrated in wealthier areas.

source.label: Ufaira and others, Frontiers in Human Dynamics, 2023

title: The grid gives way
text: Every air conditioner is running. The grid fails, water pumps stop and the district clinic loses its cooling just as heat cases arrive.

title: The bill arrives
who: A street food vendor in Bangkok
text: Her stock spoiled in the heat, and her husband’s treatment for heat exhaustion last week was paid with a loan. Tomorrow she has to work longer.

title: A death no one counts
who: An older man living alone in Chennai
text: He dies at home in a room that stayed hot all day. His death certificate will say heart failure, so it never shows up as a heat death.
